blocks.text: If you want to improve your indoor air quality, then contact our team at Rosenberg Plumbing & Air, your experts in dehumidifiers in Terrell Hills, TX. Maybe you smell a musty odor in your basement, or maybe you discovered a leak in your bathroom. Moisture in your home can lead to serious problems. Installing dehumidifiers for a house can improve your home’s air quality and prevent damage.

It may be humid outside, but that doesn’t mean it has to be humid inside. Your home may be too humid if you smell damp or musty odors. Rooms without windows, such as basements and bathrooms, are prime candidates for musty smells. If you see mold or mildew, then it’s time to install dehumidifiers for a house.

Look for these signs of high humidity in your home:Condensation on wallsCondensation on windowsDampness in one area of the homeHigher relative humidity in one area of the homeWater stains on your floors, walls, or foundation

Don’t wait to correct these issues. Excess humidity can lead to more than just discomfort. The presence of moisture over a long period of time can damage your home and lower your property value. Relative humidity levels greater than 60% can create a breeding ground for mold, which can lead to long-term health issues. Excess moisture in your home also can damage your property, including floors, carpets, linens, and more. Condensation on walls can lead to peeling paint and wallpaper. Over time, humidity can lead to rotting woodwork and moldy brick.

A dehumidifier uses a fan to pull warm, damp air into the coils. These cold coils cause the warm air to cool and contract. The coils pull water out of the air and deposit the water into a tank. Then, the dehumidifier returns cooler, dryer air to your home, reducing the relative humidity.
